Brunette is the east side of mainland New Westminster along the Brunette River / Brunette Creek corridor and Hume Park, next to the Coquitlam boundary.
This guide covers Brunette's condo buildings, townhome complexes and land: what each source verifies, the local rules, and what buyers ask.
Condo buildings in Brunette

SnapStats carries "Brunette" only under the New Westminster community (both property types), with no Brunette row under Coquitlam, and the City of New Westminster sources place it on the east side of mainland New Westminster along the Brunette River / Brunette Creek corridor and Hume Park, next to the Coquitlam boundary. Brunette Creek and Brunette Avenue also run north into Coquitlam (the Maillardville side, toward the Highway 1 Brunette Interchange) — properties north of the municipal boundary are Coquitlam, not Brunette.
Streets, schools and getting around Brunette

items.t: Brunette is the east side of mainland New Westminster along the Brunette River / Brunette Creek corridor and Hume Park, next to the Coquitlam boundary.
The housing present is single-detached homes under the RS districts on the residential streets, with industrial land along the Brunette River corridor.

Transit anchors: no SkyTrain station is inside Brunette; the nearest stations are Sapperton and Braid on the Expo Line, and TransLink route 109 (New Westminster Station / Lougheed Station) serves the East Columbia Street corridor.

Main roads: Brunette Avenue and East Columbia Street serve the area, with access toward Highway 1 at the Brunette Interchange on the Coquitlam side. Hume Park and Lower Hume Park (pool, spray park, sports fields, lacrosse box, off-leash dog park) anchor the area on the Brunette–Fraser Greenway corridor.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Brunette

items.t: Floodplain — the corridor rule: the City's floodplain study places the industrial land along the Brunette River in Floodplain Zone 4, below the Flood Construction Level, with the Brunette River running through it; the City's flood management page places sections of the mainland within the provincial floodplain, and lot-level status on the corridor is property-specific — confirm the flood construction level and an insurance quote before subjects come off on any creek-adjacent lot.

Frequent Transit Development Area: the Sapperton and Braid stations area is one of the City's Frequent Transit Development Areas in Our City 2041 — station-proximate lots may carry different expectations than interior RS-1 streets; confirm the designation for the specific parcel at the City.

items.t: A zero month is the normal shape of this sub-area's data, not a crash.
The creek crosses a city line, and the sub-area does not.

The new East Columbia supply is rental, on purpose. Premiere (72 homes, 408 East Columbia Street) is purpose-built rental and East Columbia + Strand (209 East Columbia Street) adds 99 market rental homes beside Royal Columbian Hospital and the Brewery District with anticipated occupancy Q1 2027 — new homes are arriving on this corridor, but none of them add to the condo stock a buyer can purchase.

Industrial land along the Brunette River sits in Floodplain Zone 4 below the Flood Construction Level — pull the property's flood construction level and an insurance quote before subjects come off on any creek-adjacent lot, house or strata.
The growth framework here is the station area, not a neighbourhood plan.

blocks.text: Townhome complexes in Brunette

The Brunette River/Creek corridor and Brunette Avenue run north across the boundary into Coquitlam (the Maillardville side, at the Highway 1 Brunette Interchange) — north of the boundary is Coquitlam and SD43, not New Westminster and SD40, and the one "Brunette" townhouse complex a name search surfaces (Brunette Villas) sits on the Coquitlam side. The townhouse districts are RT-2 through RT-2C (ss. 410–413) plus RT-3/3A/3B in Queensborough (ss. s. 462.14), not an RT figure.
Streets, schools and getting around Brunette

items.t: Brunette is the east-side New Westminster sub-area along the Brunette River/Creek corridor and Hume Park, hard against the Coquitlam boundary. "Brunette" is a board sub-area name; it is not a confirmed City neighbourhood-plan name — the City plans this edge through Our City 2041 (OCP Bylaw No. 7925, 2017) and the Sapperton/Braid Frequent Transit Development Area.

The corridor's land split is the defining fact: RS detached houses on the residential streets, and service-commercial / light-industrial land along Brunette Avenue under OCP Development Permit Area 6.2, Brunette Employment Lands (Bylaw 8151, 2019).

Any "Brunette median" is invented. The community figures the report does publish: New Westminster detached median $1,365,000 ($504/sqft, 94% sale-to-list, 35 days on market) and "Condos & Townhomes" combined median $560,000 ($587/sqft, 95%, 27 days on market) — community level only, cited exactly as stated, never as Brunette or townhome-only figures.

Transit: no SkyTrain station is inside Brunette; the nearest are Sapperton and Braid stations (Expo Line), and TransLink route 109 (New Westminster Station / Lougheed Station) runs on East Columbia Street at the Sapperton edge.
Schools: SD40, address-based. Per-address catchments in Brunette: run the exact address.

Amenity anchors: Hume Park and Lower Hume Park (outdoor pool, spray park, sports fields, lacrosse box, off-leash dog area) sit inside the sub-area's corridor; Royal Columbian Hospital, 330 East Columbia Street, is the regional hospital at the Sapperton edge; the library's Main Branch is at 716 6th Avenue.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Brunette

items.t: City zoning and plan — corrected districts (standing position): Zoning Bylaw No. 6680, 2001; OCP Our City 2041, Bylaw No. 7925, 2017. Townhouse districts are RT-2–RT-2C (ss. 410–413) and RT-3/3A/3B in Queensborough (ss. RT-2's published form figures: base density 18 units per net acre or FSR 0.6, height cap 25 feet, site coverage cap 40%. RS-1 (the sub-area's house zone): minimum site 557.40 m² (6,000 sq ft), FSR 0.5.

Suites as the City states them: one secondary suite per house; the City allows a property to have both a secondary suite and a laneway/carriage house (Zoning Bylaw s. 190.29 — a provision title-search and advocate sources quote; confirm the current section text in the consolidated bylaw before relying on it). Adaptable housing: at least 40% of single-storey units in multiple-unit buildings must be adaptable (Adaptable Housing Bylaw 7464, 2011).

Floodplain — the corridor's defining diligence item: the City's floodplain study places the industrial land along the Brunette River in Floodplain Zone 4, below the Flood Construction Level — the diligence question for any assembly, infill or insurance conversation on the corridor.

Property tax: City of New Westminster taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty applied July 3, 2026 and a second 5% penalty September 3, 2026. The City also runs its own electrical utility — a New Westminster–specific line item on any closing here. There is no Vancouver Empty Homes Tax in New Westminster — that 3% tax is Vancouver only and never applies here.
Presales (REDMA), if any are ever marketed here: disclosure statement (REDMA s. 18), 7-day rescission (REDMA s. 21), deposits in trust.

blocks.text: Good to know about Brunette

items.t: The sub-area's name crosses a city line the sub-area doesn't: Brunette Avenue and Brunette Creek run from New Westminster up into Coquitlam's Maillardville side — so "Brunette" search results mix two cities, two school districts and two rule books, and the only named townhouse complex in the results (Brunette Villas) is on the Coquitlam side. Basis: exclusions.

Townhouse sites in the RT-A and RT-B districts need at least 836.1 m² (9,000 sq. ft.) of site area and at least 20 m of frontage, with lane access; for most sites that means consolidating two standard lots.

A 0/0 market row is itself the market fact (dated): in September 2026 Brunette recorded no listings and no sales in either segment — the sub-area is effectively off-market for attached product, and any "Brunette townhouse" listing that appears should be boundary-checked first.

The hospital is closer than the SkyTrain: Royal Columbian Hospital (330 East Columbia Street) sits at the Sapperton edge, while the nearest stations (Sapperton, Braid) are outside the sub-area — the corridor's daily-life anchor is the hospital and Hume Park, not a station.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Brunette
Fee-simple lots

items.t: Established house lots: single-detached homes under the Single Detached Residential Districts (RS series, s.310) of Zoning Bylaw No. 6680, 2001 — RS-1 minimum site 557.40 sq. m. (6,000 sq. ft.), floor space ratio not over 0.5. These are zone figures, not a claim about any existing lot's size.

Industrial corridor land: the City's floodplain study names industrial land along the Brunette River in this sub-area — a mixed residential / creek-corridor / industrial-edge sub-area, not a uniform residential neighbourhood. That industrial land is documented as floodplain ground, never as for-sale inventory; no lot is listed, counted or priced here.

Serviced position, as the City states it: New Westminster operates its own electrical utility plus City water / sewer services. Servicing for a specific parcel is confirmed through the City's subdivision process under Bylaw No. 7142, 2007.
No ALR percentage split is stated.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Brunette

items.t: Zoning — Zoning Bylaw No. 6680, 2001: single-detached homes sit under the RS series (s.310) — RS-1 minimum site 557.40 sq. m. (6,000 sq. ft.), FSR 0.5; secondary suite and laneway / carriage house rules are set in the same bylaw.

OCP — Our City 2041, Bylaw No. 7925, 2017: the Official Community Plan governing the area; the Sapperton and Braid stations area is one of the City's Frequent Transit Development Areas, the growth framework for this edge — confirm the designation for the specific parcel at the City before promising redevelopment.

Subdivision + servicing — Bylaw No. 7142, 2007 (verified): the Subdivision and Development Control Bylaw No. 7142, 2007 requires Approving Officer approval and ensures new lots are adequately serviced and meet the Zoning Bylaw's minimum lot size and frontage requirements, through the City's pre-application / application / Works & Services Agreement process. Parcel-level standards are confirmed through that process; none is quoted here.

Flood diligence — Floodplain Zone 4 (Brunette's defining item): the City floodplain study places the industrial land along the Brunette River in Floodplain Zone 4, below the Flood Construction Level, with the Brunette River running through it. Zone 4 belongs to Brunette only in this ledger — it is not Queensborough's Zone 1, the Quay/Downtown's Zone 3, or North Arm's Zone 2.

Strata block: Form B diligence (provided within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page); depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws void since November 24, 2022 (short-term restrictions may still apply by bylaw); only 55+ age bylaws valid under SPA ss.123.1/123.2, with May 1, 2023 exemptions; a listing's "45+" line is not a valid BC age bylaw.

ALR rules (for completeness — no Brunette ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an error.

New Westminster property taxes: 2026 property taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty on current taxes remaining unpaid on July 3, 2026 and a second 5% penalty on any unpaid balance on September 3, 2026.

blocks.text: Good to know about Brunette

items.t: The zero month is the market fact: Brunette is a small, thinly traded sub-area where listings appear irregularly — September 2026's 0/0 in both segments is documented in SnapStats, and any sub-area statistic quoted for that month is invented.

The city line runs through the creek corridor: Brunette Avenue / Brunette Creek addresses north of the municipal boundary are Coquitlam (Maillardville side) — wrong-city paperwork, taxes and school district all turn on that line. Parks and Open Space.pdf
The city runs its own power: New Westminster operates its own electrical utility alongside City water and sewer — a servicing and closing-adjustment difference from every neighbouring municipality.
